subject: Forensic readiness & audit-data portability: exportability questions
content:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@epochfinancial.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@epochfinancial.com, legalhold@epochfinancial.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFP: Audit logs, retention windows, exportability (Epoch Financial)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for engaging with Epoch. As part of our RFP for platform preservation and forensics we need clear, actionable answers to the audit log / retention / exportability section. We've attached our questionnaire (short list) — please confirm answers and the SLA for bulk export and legal-hold handoffs. High level asks:

1) What exact audit events are recorded (auth, token lifecycle, model inference inputs/outputs, admin actions, network access)? Are logs immutable/append-only?
2) Retention windows: default, extended, and legal-hold. Can retention be configured per-tenant?
3) Export formats: schema and compression (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV). Can exports include full model inputs/outputs and KV cache traces?
4) Tamper-evidence / chain-of-custody: cryptographic checksums, signed manifests, and time-stamped receipts?
5) Time to produce a complete bulk export for a 6-month slice (50M events) and for expedited legal-hold export?
6) Redaction & PII handling: options for tokenization, selective export, and redaction markers in exports.
7) Proof of delivery: S3 delivery vs secure download link vs direct transfer to customer bucket.

Please see the attached questionnaire (epoch_rfp_audit_questions.docx). We need a written response and an exportability runbook or example manifest for the legal team.

Regards,
Sam Wong
Head of Security Ops
Epoch Financial

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: Audit logs, retention windows, exportability (Epoch Financial)

Sam — thanks for the clear list and the doc. I've looped in Markus (runtime engineering) and Jordan (platform ops) so we can give both product-level commitments and operational timelines.

Short answer/high level: Redwood supports comprehensive audit capture (auth, admin, model calls including metadata for inputs/outputs by default), append-only immutable storage for audit records, per-tenant retention configuration, multiple export formats (gzipped NDJSON preferred for forensic fidelity; Parquet for analytics), tamper-evidence via SHA-256 manifests and signed delivery receipts, and standard delivery options including controlled S3 handoff. For legal holds we offer an expedited path.

Next steps: we'll produce a written RFP response and an export runbook. Estimated delivery: initial written answers + playbook draft by Mon 2026-08-23; sample export manifest and a pinned-playbook PDF attached for reference.

Key attachments: redwood_forensic_playbook_v2.pdf (playbook: export schema, manifest format, chain-of-custody steps), export_request_template.json (request template you can use to open exports).

I'll capture specifics below from Markus for the technical details you asked for.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@epochfinancial.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP: Audit logs, retention windows, exportability (Epoch Financial)

Hi Sam — adding the technical detail Grace promised. Answers below map to your numbered questions. If you'd like, we can include snippets from a one-off export so your legal/forensics team can validate the manifest structure.

1) Events captured:
   - Authentication events (login/refresh/revoke), admin IAM actions (role changes, permission grants), model invocation metadata (model id, version, prompt hash, token counts), inference telemetry (latency, compute node id), and optional payload capture: full prompt and response stored as encrypted blobs if requested in account settings.
   - Network / infra-level events such as peering configs are captured in separate infra logs and linked via request-id.

   Storage: audit events are written to an append-only ledger backed by object storage with write-once lifecycle and immutable manifests. Each object includes a block-level SHA-256 and we store a signed manifest chain for tamper evidence.

2) Retention windows:
   - Default: 90 days for full payloads (inputs/outputs), 365 days for metadata and indices.
   - Extended: configurable to custom durations (30d/90d/1y/3y/indefinite) per-tenant via policy APIs.
   - Legal hold: can pin records indefinitely; legal holds are applied at the account or dataset level and prevent lifecycle deletion.

3) Export formats and contents:
   - Supported formats: gzipped NDJSON (recommended for forensics), Parquet (columnar analytics), and CSV (index-only exports).
   - Export payloads: forensics exports can include full encrypted blobs (prompt and response), metadata index (user id, request-id, model version, timestamp), and optional KV cache traces for sessions where we capture ephemeral state.
   - Schema: see redwood_forensic_playbook_v2.pdf page 12 for the NDJSON schema (fields: event_id, ts, tenant_id, user_id, action, model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, prompt_blob_ref, response_blob_ref, checksum, redaction_flags).

4) Tamper-evidence / chain-of-custody:
   - Each export bundle includes: gzipped payload(s), manifest.json with per-file SHA-256, a signed top-level manifest signed by Redwood's export key, and a delivery receipt (timestamped and signed). We can optionally include a notarized timestamp via a third-party TSA at the customer's request.

5) Timing / SLA for exports:
   - Standard bulk export SLA: 14 business days for up to 100M events (delivered as staged S3 objects to the customer bucket).
   - Expedited legal-hold export: 3 business days for up to 25M events (additional premium may apply).
   - For very large datasets or forensics requiring on-prem transfer, schedule-based transfer windows and parallel multipart delivery apply; Jordan can coordinate throughput and IAM setup.

6) Redaction & PII handling:
   - Options: (a) pre-export tokenization (replace sensitive fields with stable tokens), (b) export-level redaction flags (include redaction markers but omit payload), (c) full payload export with inline-redaction markers and a companion redaction map.
   - We support field-level redaction policies via the platform policy API; customers can supply a policy spec and choose to keep original encrypted blobs in a sealed bucket for judicial review.

7) Delivery options / proof of delivery:
   - Standard: S3 PUT to a customer-supplied bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS), pre-signed HTTPS download link (30-day window) as fallback, or secure transfer (SFTP) for special cases.
   - Proof: delivery manifest, signed delivery receipt, and object-level checksums; optional cross-account replication record.

Operational notes:
   - Access controls: export requests require dual-approval (requestor + security approver) and are logged as auditable events.
   - Sample manifest and NDJSON schema are attached in the playbook; export_request_template.json can be used to open a run in our Ops portal.
   - Costs: bulk export pricing is usage-tiered (we can propose a one-time export fee + per-GB egress).

If you need extracts for a discovery set (narrow time windows + filters), we can provide samples within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference
